references.text: Peace offerings (שְׁלָמִים) are a fundamental type of sacrifice described in Leviticus, and Numbers 7:88 summarizes all the peace offerings given at the altar's dedication.
Detailed laws concerning peace offerings that form the basis for the sacrifices mentioned in Numbers 7:88.
The dedication of the altar at Sinai, which parallels the dedication (חֲנֻכַּת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ) mentioned in Numbers 7:88.
Moses anoints and consecrates the altar, referring to 'after it was anointed' (אַחֲרֵי הִמָּשַׁח אֹתוֹ) in Numbers 7:88.
The anointing of the altar as part of the dedication process, linked to the phrase 'after it was anointed' in Numbers 7:88.
Solomon's offering of peace sacrifices at the temple dedication, a similar grand consecration ceremony like that in Numbers 7:88.
A parallel to Solomon's temple dedication with massive peace offerings, reflecting the dedication in Numbers 7:88.
The dedication of the second temple with sacrifices, including peace offerings, which parallels the altar dedication in Numbers 7:88.
